title: Mordecai
lead: Mordecai son of Jair, a Benjaminite at the Persian court in Susa, raised his cousin Esther, refused to bow to Haman, and rose to be second to King Ahasuerus. With Esther he set up the feast of Purim.

sections.h: Mordecai in the Bible and after
sections.b: Mordecai is introduced as "a Jewish man" of the tribe of Benjamin, descended from Kish, and linked to the exile of Jeconiah (Esther 2:5–6). He sits in the king's gate, uncovers a plot against the king (Esther 2:21–23), will not bow to Haman (Esther 3:2), and urges Esther to speak for her people (Esther 4:13–14). He is honored in Haman's place (Esther 6), receives the king's ring (Esther 8:2), writes the letters of Purim (Esther 9:20) and ends the book as the second man after the king (Esther 10:3). The name is built on that of the Babylonian god Marduk; a Persian official named Marduka appears in tablets from Persepolis, though whether he is this man is debated. A Mordecai also appears in the lists of returnees (Ezra 2:2; Nehemiah 7:7), a different man as most readers take it. 2 Maccabees 15:36 calls Purim "Mordecai's day".
